title: Microsoft IQ: Foundry IQ, Fabric IQ and Work IQ

sentences.text: Tuesday morning at Contoso.
The HR agent gets three questions.
An employee asks about the parental leave policy.
The sales director asks for revenue by region.
A manager asks which meetings this week mention a renewal.
None of these answers lives in Copilot Studio.
The policy, the numbers and the meetings are kept by other teams, on other platforms.
By the end of this class you will know which Microsoft I Q capability answers each one.
Here is the picture to keep.
Microsoft I Q is like three expert colleagues sitting next to your agent.
The first one knows the official policies.
The second one knows the business numbers.
The third one knows how your teams work every day, their files, email, meetings and chats.
Your agent does not learn what they know.
It asks them.
Their names are Foundry I Q, Fabric I Q and Work I Q.
The key idea is reuse.
With a knowledge source, you pick and upload the content yourself in Copilot Studio.
With an I Q capability, the context already exists outside Copilot Studio, and someone else maintains it on another platform.
Your agent simply points to it, and you can select only the items you have access to.
Note that Fabric I Q and Work I Q are still in preview.
Where do these colleagues join the agent?
On the Microsoft Copilot harness, which until late October was called the GitHub Copilot harness.
Same harness, new name, so the exam may still use the old one.
You open the Build tab and add each capability as a tool, in Tools.
The orchestrator then decides when to call it, based only on the tool's name and description.
Foundry I Q is the policy expert.
It brings curated knowledge, such as policies and authoritative documents, from a knowledge base built in Microsoft Foundry.
Remember two exam facts.
An agent can have only one Foundry I Q connection.
And the connection uses one of four authentication types: A P I key, client certificate, service principal, or Microsoft Entra I D integrated.
Every type needs the Foundry I Q search service endpoint.
Your turn.
The HR agent uses Foundry I Q, but its answers about leave are strange and incomplete.
Where do you fix it?
By removing the connection and adding it again?
In Copilot Studio, by editing the agent instructions?
Or in Microsoft Foundry, together with the knowledge base owner?
Decide before I answer.
You tune it in Microsoft Foundry, with the owner.
The knowledge base lives there, and removing the connection in Copilot Studio does not change it at all.
Because the orchestrator chooses tools from their descriptions, a vague description is a real problem.
Two tools may both claim the same question, or neither one gets called.
So rewrite every description in three parts.
When to use it.
What it returns.
And what it does not handle.
For example: use for H R policy questions, returns policy text, does not handle salaries or personal data.
Fabric I Q, in preview, is the numbers expert.
It grounds your agent in the Microsoft Fabric semantic model, with its measures, hierarchies and dimensions.
Because the agent uses that model, you do not rebuild the same metrics or data models in Copilot Studio.
Revenue by region already exists in Fabric, so the agent reuses it.
You need an agent on the Microsoft Copilot harness and access to the Fabric workspace and semantic model.
How do you know it worked?
Open the Preview tab, keep End user preview off, ask a test question and read the activity trace step by step.
If there is no Fabric I Q call, check Tools and the description.
If a different tool was called, the borders between descriptions need to be clearer.
If you see an error, it is often a failed authentication, so check that the tool's credentials are current.
Your turn.
You ask the agent for revenue by region.
The activity trace shows that the policy tool was called instead of Fabric I Q.
What do you change?
Make the tool descriptions clearer about what each one handles?
Remove Fabric I Q and use a knowledge source?
Or rebuild the revenue metrics inside Copilot Studio?
Decide before I answer.
Clarify the descriptions.
The orchestrator picked the wrong tool because the borders were vague.
Work I Q, in preview, is the teamwork expert.
It gives the agent context about how people work in Microsoft three six five: files, email, meetings and chats.
You add it as a Model Context Protocol tool, an M C P tool.
And it is read-only, unless an administrator turns on write operations in the Microsoft three six five admin center.
Reading is the default.
Writing is a deliberate admin choice.
Work I Q also needs some admin work first.
A Global Administrator enables it once for the whole tenant.
The tenant needs a usage based billing plan in Copilot Studio.
And admins create a separate spending policy for Work I Q usage.
One more limit: every M C P server counts toward the agent's tool total, and extra servers are skipped for a turn, so keep the number of attached servers small.
Your turn.
A maker wants meeting and email context.
Instead of Work I Q, they add the separate Mail, Teams and OneDrive tools.
Is that the recommended choice?
Is it required, because Work I Q cannot read email?
Is it wrong, because those tools are a legacy experience on the standard harness and billing?
Or is it fine, because they read the same data?
Decide before I answer.
It is the legacy path.
Use Work I Q instead.
So how do you choose?
Ask who maintains the context.
Policies tuned by another team point to Foundry I Q.
Business measures in a Fabric semantic model point to Fabric I Q.
Email, files and meetings point to Work I Q.
Documents you write and update yourself fit a normal knowledge source.
And a whole domain run by another Copilot Studio agent fits a connected agent.
Here are the steps.
Open your agent on the Microsoft Copilot harness and go to the Build tab.
In Tools, select Add a tool.
For Foundry I Q, create a new connection, pick the authentication type, enter the search service endpoint and choose the knowledge base.
For Fabric I Q, select it and add it.
For Work I Q, go to M C P and pick Work I Q.
Then rewrite each description and test in Preview.
Your turn.
The sales director wants revenue by region, and those measures are already modelled in a Fabric semantic model.
Which capability should the agent use?
A knowledge source with an exported spreadsheet?
Work I Q, because the director asks in a Teams chat?
Or Fabric I Q, because the measures live in the semantic model?
Decide before I answer.
Fabric I Q.
The numbers expert reuses the model, so nobody copies or rebuilds the metrics.
Back to Tuesday at Contoso.
The leave policy comes from Foundry I Q, tuned by the compliance team in Foundry.
Revenue by region comes from Fabric I Q and the existing semantic model.
The renewal meetings come from Work I Q, read-only because the admin did not enable writes.
Remember for the exam: one Foundry I Q connection, Work I Q is an M C P tool, and you choose by who maintains the context.
